cutoff_window.rule: Include only public web sources published or visibly updated within the last 2 days relative to run time; exclude missing, ambiguous, future-dated, or boundary-only dates.

qualifying_findings.title: GitHub describes repository instructions, skills, custom agents, and MCP as project-context layers for Copilot
qualifying_findings.date_basis: Article byline date visible on page.
qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: GitHub published guidance explaining how repository custom instructions, path-specific instruction files, agent skills, custom agents, and MCP servers can provide Copilot with project conventions, repeatable procedures, specialized roles, and external tool access.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Supports local guidance that durable instructions, task-specific skills, specialized agents, and governed MCP tools should be separate context layers rather than one overloaded prompt.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication: Refresh durable instruction layering, agent-skill packaging, and MCP-governance leaves with a routing note instead of duplicating Copilot product coverage.

qualifying_findings.title: ASE JAWs presentation reports measured benefit and cost increase from adding an agent skill to code review
qualifying_findings.date_basis: Conference program lists the session time as Mon 12 Oct 2026 14:09-14:14.
qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: The abstract says the authors compare an unconfigured agent with an agent equipped with a code-review skill using the c-CRAB evaluation protocol. The skill-equipped configuration improves executable-oracle pass rate from 30.59% to 34.12% while increasing average cost from $1.01 to $2.42 per task.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Gives practice-level evidence that skills may improve review usefulness but should be evaluated against cost, runtime, and task-specific outcome metrics.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication: Use skill-based code-review improvements as a measured practice claim only when paired with cost and executable-oracle evidence.

qualifying_findings.title: aicodereview.io publishes GitLab-specific AI code-review evaluation checklist
qualifying_findings.date_basis: Article header date visible on page.
qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: The guide argues that GitLab support should be evaluated through host-specific write-back behavior, draft-review persistence, suggestion application, merge controls, large-MR context loss, correction carry-over, self-managed setup, and admin-token requirements.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Turns AI-review tool selection into a workflow-compatibility and evidence-gathering exercise instead of a generic product ranking.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication: Add or refresh AI-review rollout checklists so host integration, self-managed deployment, identity attribution, and write-back limits are tested on the team's actual merge-request platform.

qualifying_findings.title: Atlantic essay frames AI-assisted personal software as expert-directed high-level programming rather than pure vibe coding
qualifying_findings.date_basis: Article header date and time visible on page.
qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: Ian Bogost describes building personal software with AI assistance and argues that calling the process vibe coding mischaracterizes expert-directed high-level programming. The essay contrasts personally useful software with pressure to turn small programs into platform-style applications.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Useful as an adoption lens: AI-assisted coding changes who can create local software, but teams still need product-boundary judgment and should not equate prompting with completed engineering.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication: Potential support for pages that distinguish personal automation, internal tools, productization pressure, and human product judgment in AI-assisted delivery.

qualifying_findings.title: iTechGuides recommends bounded AI review tasks and explicit human review ownership
qualifying_findings.date_basis: Article header date visible on page.
qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: The article says AI can help draft review feedback or propose responses, but faster review does not prove safer code. It recommends bounded, reversible pilots, measuring speed with usefulness and quality, and keeping a named human responsible for merge decisions.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Reinforces local review-governance rules: AI review is input to human judgment, not a replacement for context ownership or readiness decisions.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication: Could update intelligent-code-review.md and layered-ai-code-review-roles.md with bounded-task and human-owner language.
qualifying_findings.follow_up_notes: Source contains advertising blocks; retain only factual practice claims and cited research references during ingest.

qualifying_findings.title: iTechGuides publishes a small AI code-review smoke-test pattern and warns against ranking claims
qualifying_findings.date_basis: Article header date visible on page.
qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: The article describes a five-case review smoke test covering off-by-one, resource cleanup, swallowed database exception, race condition, and path traversal cases. It says the suite can probe specific bug classes but cannot rank models or replace manual review, and notes keyword scoring limitations.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Supports keeping AI-review checks as scoped regression probes with manual interpretation, not broad claims of reviewer quality.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication: Candidate evidence for lightweight smoke-test examples under code-review evals and rubrics.
qualifying_findings.follow_up_notes: During ingest, avoid adopting the article's product ads or anecdotal run as durable benchmark evidence.

qualifying_findings.title: Kunal Ganglani argues evaluation, permission boundaries, memory expiry, and measurement must precede agent orchestration
qualifying_findings.date_basis: Article footer and citation block show written date.
qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: The article endorses context, tools, memory, orchestration, and evaluation as useful concepts, but argues security, cost, team-workflow impact, evaluation-first practice, MCP approval gates, memory expiry, and instrumentation are necessary for real development workflows.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Matches local guidance that coding-agent adoption is a system design problem with permissions, eval harnesses, memory scope, and operational metrics.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication: Could strengthen evaluation-first ordering and memory-expiry caveats in agent workflow and context architecture leaves.
qualifying_findings.follow_up_notes: Use as practitioner synthesis; verify any IBM-specific source separately before ingesting the IBM framing.

qualifying_findings.title: NeuryCode recommends repo-specific code-review skills and warns about built-in skill name collisions
qualifying_findings.date_basis: Article header date visible on page.
qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: The article argues that built-in code-review skills cannot know repository-specific dependencies, ignored concerns, compliance context, release cadence, or risk profile. It describes a case where a custom skill named code-review was replaced by a built-in command behavior and says renaming the skill restored the expected reviewer behavior.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Adds a concrete operational risk: skill naming and loading precedence can silently change reviewer behavior, so repositories need explicit naming, ownership, and review-skill provenance.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication: Candidate update for repository-configured AI review and durable-instruction pages: review skills need unique names, scoped loading, and collision checks.
qualifying_findings.follow_up_notes: Treat vendor-specific claims about exactly which files each tool reads as volatile; verify from official docs before durable synthesis.

qualifying_findings.title: iTechGuides distinguishes AI review findings from verification evidence
qualifying_findings.date_basis: Article header date visible on page.
qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: The article says AI review outputs are claims to evaluate, while verification evidence should say which checks ran, what they covered, their results, and what was not checked. It warns against broad claims such as an agent verified a change unless the scope is explicit.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Directly supports local evidence-package language: completion claims should distinguish review findings, test results, linter scope, security reproduction attempts, and unchecked areas.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication: Candidate for verification-loops-and-evals.md, ai-code-evidence-packages.md, and pre-pr-independent-review.md.
qualifying_findings.follow_up_notes: Verify product-specific examples from official docs before adding them as product facts.

qualifying_findings.title: Pondero summarizes a Harvard/Jellyfish study as a review-capacity warning for coding-agent adoption
qualifying_findings.date_basis: Article header date visible on page.
qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: The summary reports that a Harvard working paper using Jellyfish data found agentic tools increased lines of code, commits, and pull requests but did not measurably increase resolved Jira issues or epics, with pull-request review time rising. The underlying working paper version is dated August 4, 2026, so the fresh item is the secondary practice framing rather than the primary study.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Useful as a routing note for adoption metrics: agent-seat business cases should include review capacity and shipped-work outcomes, not only code volume.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication: Could inform operating-model pages that measure accepted changes, review load, and issue throughput rather than generated LOC.
qualifying_findings.follow_up_notes: Before ingesting the study itself, collect the primary working paper separately and mark its older date.
